newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium sector seen needing more smelter capacity.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium sector seen needing more smelter capacity.

text.p: The global aluminium industry is facing a shortfall of nearly one million tonnes of primary smelting capacity by the year 2000, consultant CRU International said in a report.
But the industry should be wary of expanding too fast, even though about 11 million tonnes of new capacity will be needed over the next 15 years, it added.

"High prices are likely to accompany this capacity squeeze and the industry will have to guard against its historical tendency to over-invest in greenfield smelters as this would result in a prolonged period of structural over-capacity," CRU said.
At least 2.4 million tonnes of the required 11 million tonnes will materialise through so-called "capacity creep", the process of improvements within existing smelters.
For example, at Kaiser Aluminum Corp's Mead smelter in the United States, commissioned in the 1940s and 1950s, potline capacity has increased by nearly two thirds.
The capital cost of adding capacity through "capacity creep" is usually 60 percent less per tonne than through greenfield and brownfield investments.
Investors should avoid over-estimating the number of permanent smelter closures, CRU said.
"Technological advances mean emissions from Soderberg smelters can now be reduced to acceptable levels and the deregulation of the electricity sector is reducing costs in many cases," it said.
Less than 50,000 tonnes of annual capacity will close before 2010 because producers can gain more value from investing in so-called vulnerable smelters, CRU added.
